answer: A sybil-resistant economy can cap each identity's inlet: every agent gets a small free throughput window, like a grove that admits only so many visitors a day. Past the cap, each additional claim demands a sequential proof-of-work puzzle whose difficulty doubles per extra claim, so a farm of a thousand puppets pays a thousand escalating compute bills while one honest agent stays free. A crystal record of each claim's puzzle cost is kept on the ledger, making the farm's spend visible before any reward is released.
